tan θ = sin θ / cos θ

sec θ = 1 / cos θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ (11/12)² + cos²θ = 1

⇒ 121/144 + cos²θ

questions.question: Evaluate (9 sin θ + 2 cos θ) / (9 sin θ − 2 cos θ), if 3 tan θ = 4.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given 3 tan θ = 4 ⇒ **tan θ = 4/3**.

Divide the numerator and denominator by **cos θ** to convert the expression into **tan θ**.

Expression = (9 tan θ + 2) / (9 tan θ − 2)

Substitute tan θ = 4/3 ⇒ (9 × 4/3 + 2) / (9 × 4/3 − 2) = (12 + 2) / (12 − 2) = 14 / 10 = 7/5.

**∴ The correct answer is 7/5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b835276e017eccb7f8ad43e053256e0624e7510905e9c758f78d40128929e4dd.png] 

**Given:** 3 tan θ = 4

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base; sin θ = P/H; cos θ = B/H

⇒ tan θ = 4/3

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 4, Base (B) = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse (H) = √(P² + B²) = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5

⇒ sin θ = 4/5 and cos θ = 3/5

⇒ (9 × 4/5 + 2 × 3/5) / (9 × 4/5 − 2 × 3/5)

⇒ (36/5 + 6/5) / (36/5 − 6/5) = (42/5) / (30/5)

⇒ 42 / 30 = 7/5

**∴ The correct answer is 7/5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Fundamental ratios are sin θ = P/H, cos θ = B/H, and tan θ = P/B.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers (a, b, c) such that a² + b² = c². Common triplets include (3, 4, 5) and (5, 12, 13).

Ratio Transformation

An expression involving sin θ and cos θ of the same degree can be simplified by dividing by cos θ or sin θ to convert it into tan θ or cot θ.</p

questions.question: if cot θ = (15)/(8), θ is an acute angle, then find the value of ((1-costheta)(2+2costheta))/((2-2sintheta)(1+sintheta)).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the expression using the **identity** (1 − cos² θ) = sin² θ and (1 − sin² θ) = cos² θ.

Expression = [2(1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] ÷ [2(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] = (1 − cos² θ) ÷ (1 − sin² θ).

This simplifies directly to sin² θ ÷ cos² θ = **tan² θ**.

Since **cot θ = 15/8**, then **tan θ = 8/15**.

Result = (8/15)² = 64/225.

**∴ The correct answer is 64/225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cot θ = 15/8, where θ is an **acute angle**.

In a **right-angled triangle**, cot θ = Base / Perpendicular.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d920d688ab52d66c861be460861d79b9a424d144c2d1101f8943a2d144dac49.png] 

Using **Pythagoras Theorem**: H² = P² + B² ⇒ H² = 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 ⇒ **H = 17**.

**Formula Used:** (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

Expression = ((1 − cos θ)(2 + 2 cos θ)) / ((2 − 2 sin θ)(1 + sin θ))

⇒ [2 × (1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ)] / [2 × (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)]

⇒ (1 − cos² θ) / (1 − sin² θ)

By **trigonometric identities**: 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ and 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ

⇒ sin² θ / cos² θ = tan² θ

⇒ (1 / cot θ)²

⇒ (1 / (15/8))² = (8/15)²

⇒ 64 / 225

**∴ The correct answer is 64/225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | 2. 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ | 3. 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Relations

tan θ = 1 / cot θ, sec θ = 1 / cos θ, and cosec θ = 1 / sin θ.

Pythagorean Triplet

For a right-angled triangle with sides (8, 15, 17), the square of the largest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (17² = 8² + 15²).</p

questions.question: Find the value of tan 3θ if sec 3θ = cosec (4θ - 15°).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sec 3θ = cosec (4θ - 15°)

**Calculations:**

According to question,

sec 3θ = cosec (4θ - 15)

⇒ cosec (90° - 3θ) = cosec (4θ – 15°)

⇒ 90° - 3θ = 4θ - 15°

⇒ 7θ = 90° + 15°

⇒ θ = 105°/7 = 15°

so, tan3θ 

= tan(3 × 15°) 

= tan45°

= 1

**Hence, The Required value is 1.**

questions.question: If sec θ + tan θ = 3, then what is the value of sec θ - tan θ ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The trigonometric identity is **sec² θ − tan² θ = 1**.

This can be factored as **(sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1**.

This implies that **(sec θ + tan θ)** and **(sec θ − tan θ)** are **reciprocals** of each other.

Given **sec θ + tan θ = 3**, then **sec θ − tan θ = 1/3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec θ + tan θ = 3

**Formula Used:** **sec² θ − tan² θ = 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/494e3e53811ee8e902d4f9e228508aff12f3ae485d3a38fb27b558eadf4070d4.png] 

⇒ We know that **sec² θ − tan² θ = 1**

⇒ Using **a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)**

⇒ **(sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1**

⇒ Substitute the given value: **3 × (sec θ − tan θ) = 1**

⇒ **sec θ − tan θ = 1/3**

**∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Identities

There are three fundamental identities: **sin² θ + cos² θ = 1**, **sec² θ − tan² θ = 1**, and **cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1**.

Cosecant and Cotangent Relationship

Similar to secant and tangent, if **cosec θ + cot θ = x**, then **cosec θ − cot θ = 1/x**.

Determining Individual Values

By adding or subtracting these equations, we can find **sec θ = (x + 1/x) / 2** and **tan θ = (x − 1/x) / 2**.</p

frac{[8 sin {A}+11 operatorname{cosec} {A}-cot ² {A}]}{10 cos 2 {A}}

questions.question: If sin x – cos x = 0, 0° < x < 90° then the value of (sec x + cosec x)² is:
If tan x = (7)/(5), then the value of (9 sin x - frac{42)/(5)cos x}{15 sin x + 21 cos x} is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the **numerator** and **denominator** by **cos x** to convert the expression into **tan x**.

Given **tan x = 7/5**.

Expression = [9(7/5) − 42/5] ÷ [15(7/5) + 21] = [63/5 − 42/5] ÷ [21 + 21]

Expression = [21/5] ÷ 42 = 21 ÷ (5 × 42) = 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fbbdc1b4f04ae5d67060f19a7ba95fdc65b9d83c9001b928a7d81eda4e849c8.png] 

**Given:** tan x = 7/5

**Formula Used:** Expression = (9 sin x − (42/5) cos x) ÷ (15 sin x + 21 cos x)

⇒ Divide every term by **cos x**:

⇒ Value = [9(sin x/cos x) − (42/5)(cos x/cos x)] ÷ [15(sin x/cos x) + 21(cos x/cos x)]

⇒ Value = [9 tan x − 42/5] ÷ [15 tan x + 21]

⇒ Substitute tan x = 7/5:

⇒ Value = [9 × (7/5) − 42/5] ÷ [15 × (7/5) + 21]

⇒ Value = [63/5 − 42/5] ÷ [21 + 21]

⇒ Value = [21/5] ÷ 42

⇒ Value = 21 ÷ (5 × 42) = 1/10 = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratio Transformation

For expressions involving only sin x and cos x in a linear ratio, divide by cos x to utilize tan x directly without finding the hypotenuse.

Fundamental Identity

tan x = sin x ÷ cos x and cot x = cos x ÷ sin x.

Pythagorean Triplets

In a right triangle, p² + b² = h². For 7 and 5, h = √(49+25) = √74.</p

questions.question: Evaluate the given expression: (5)/(1 + cot²theta) + (3)/(1 + tan²theta) + 2cos²theta
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 45° in the given expression.

We know cot 45° = 1, tan 45° = 1, and cos 45° = 1/√2.

⇒ Expression = 5 / (1 + 1²) + 3 / (1 + 1²) + 2 × (1/√2)²

⇒ Expression = 5/2 + 3/2 + 2 × (1/2)

⇒ Expression = 8/2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 5 / (1 + cot²θ) + 3 / (1 + tan²θ) + 2cos²θ

**Formula Used:**

1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ

1 / cosecθ = sinθ

1 / secθ = cosθ

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ 5 / cosec²θ + 3 / sec²θ + 2cos²θ

⇒ 5sin²θ + 3cos²θ + 2cos²θ

⇒ 5sin²θ + 5cos²θ

⇒ 5 × (sin²θ + cos²θ)

⇒ 5 × 1 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

sinθ = 1 / cosecθ, cosθ = 1 / secθ, and tanθ = 1 / cotθ.

Value Substitution Method

For expressions independent of θ, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, or 90° directly yields the answer, provided no term becomes undefined.
</p

questions.question: Simplify the following expression: {1-sin Aover cos A}+{cos A over 1-sin A}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute **A = 30°** in the given expression:

sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 30° = √3/2

Value = (1 − 0.5)/(√3/2) + (√3/2)/(1 − 0.5) = (1/2)/(√3/2) + (√3/2)/(1/2) = 1/√3 + √3

Value = (1 + 3)/√3 = 4/√3

Checking options: 2 sec 30° = 2 × (2/√3) = 4/√3. Match found.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 sec A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** {(1 − sin A)/cos A} + {cos A/(1 − sin A)}

**Formula Used:** sin²A + cos²A = 1 and 1/cos A = sec A

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77d73660c3d7e7af333c7bddf2979d4f22ba7d468e2e24f8c113948bd1c3b092.png] 

⇒ Take LCM of the denominators: cos A × (1 − sin A)

⇒ Numerator = (1 − sin A)² + cos²A

⇒ Expanding numerator: (1 − 2 sin A + sin²A) + cos²A

⇒ Using identity sin²A + cos²A = 1, we get: 1 − 2 sin A + 1

⇒ Numerator = 2 − 2 sin A = 2(1 − sin A)

⇒ Expression = [2(1 − sin A)] ÷ [cos A(1 − sin A)]

⇒ Expression = 2 / cos A = 2 sec A

**∴ The correct answer is 2 sec A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Secant is the reciprocal of cosine (sec θ = 1/cos θ) and Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine (cosec θ = 1/sin θ).

Value Substitution Method

For simplification questions, substituting standard angles like 0°, 30°, 45° or 60° can quickly verify the correct option.</p

questions.question: If √2 sin (60° – α) = 1, 0° < α < 90°, then α is equal to:
If frac{{sin A + cos A}}{{cos A}} = frac{{17}}{{12}}, then the value of frac{{1 - cos A}}{{sin A}} is:
Evaluate frac{sin 54circ}{cos 36circ}+frac{sec 46circ}{operatorname{cosec} 44circ}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **54° + 36° = 90°**, we have **sin 54° = cos 36°** ⇒ sin 54° ÷ cos 36° = 1.

Similarly, since **46° + 44° = 90°**, we have **sec 46° = cosec 44°** ⇒ sec 46° ÷ cosec 44° = 1.

Thus, the value of the expression is 1 + 1 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression to evaluate: (sin 54° ÷ cos 36°) + (sec 46° ÷ cosec 44°)

**Formula Used:**

Complementary angle trigonometric relations:

⇒ **sin θ = cos(90° − θ)**

⇒ **sec θ = cosec(90° − θ)**

**Calculations:**

Expressing the angles in terms of their complements:

⇒ sin 54° = sin(90° − 36°) = cos 36°

⇒ sec 46° = sec(90° − 44°) = cosec 44°

Substituting these equivalent values into the given expression:

⇒ (cos 36° ÷ cos 36°) + (cosec 44° ÷ cosec 44°)

⇒ 1 + 1

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles Rule

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles satisfy: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Reciprocal Identities

cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ, sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ, and cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.</p

questions.question: If 6 Cot θ = 5, then find the value of (6 cos θ + sin θ)/(6 cos θ - 4 sin θ)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given that **6 cot θ = 5**, we can simplify the required expression.

Divide both the numerator and the denominator by **sin θ** to convert the terms into **cot θ**.

Expression = (6 cot θ + 1) / (6 cot θ − 4)

Substitute **6 cot θ = 5** directly: (5 + 1) / (5 − 4) = 6 / 1 = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 6 cot θ = 5

**Formula Used:** cot θ = Base / Perpendicular = cos θ / sin θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5378fa034db30f5c2fad89a6c9f09e8d145565bf33c94101f7549e52e85fe707.png] 

⇒ 6 cot θ = 5 ⇒ **cot θ = 5/6**

⇒ Since cot θ = cos θ / sin θ, we can assume **cos θ = 5k** and **sin θ = 6k**.

⇒ Required value = (6 cos θ + sin θ) / (6 cos θ − 4 sin θ)

⇒ Substituting the values: [6(5k) + 6k] / [6(5k) − 4(6k)]

⇒ Value = (30k + 6k) / (30k − 24k)

⇒ Value = 36k / 6k = 6

The calculated result 6 matches Option 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratio Identities

The fundamental quotient identity for cotangent is **cot θ = cos θ / sin θ** and for tangent is **tan θ = sin θ / cos θ**.

Reciprocal Relationships

The cotangent function is the reciprocal of the tangent function: **cot θ = 1 / tan θ**.

Pythagorean Identity

Another important identity involving cotangent is **1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ**.</p

questions.question: triangleABC is a right-angle triangle at B and tan A = (3)/(4), then sin A + sin B + sin C will be equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC is a right-angle triangle at B and tan A = (3)/(4)

Concept used:

1. tan θ = Height ÷ Base

2. sin θ = Height ÷ Hypotenuse

3. Pythagoras theorem states that “In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse side is equal to the sum of squares of the other two sides“.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9cd168c6cf1b93429926d1e105c2f10de886318d18b551cb29007219e81714a0.png] 

tan A = (3)/(4)

⇒ frac {BC}{AB} = (3)/(4)

⇒ BC : AB = 3 : 4

Let the measure of BC and AB be 3k and 4k respectively.

​According to the concept,

AC² = sqrt { (3k)² + (4k)² } = 5k

Now, sin A + sin B + sin C

⇒ frac {BC}{AC} + sin 90^circ + frac {AB}{AC}

⇒ frac {BC + AB}{AC} + 1

⇒ frac {3k + 4k}{5k} + 1

⇒ frac {7}{5} + 1

⇒ frac {12}{5} = 2(2)/(5)

**∴ The value of sin A + sin B + sin C is 2(2)/(5).**

questions.question: If sin(A + B) = √3/2 and tan(A – B) = 1/√3, then (2A + 3B) is equal to∶
For what value of t is the value of sin²(t), half of the value of tan(t)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For trigonometric equations, substituting the options directly is the fastest approach.

Let's check Option 2 where t = 45°.

LHS = sin²(45°) = (1/√2)² = 1/2

RHS = 1/2 × tan(45°) = 1/2 × 1 = 1/2

Since LHS = RHS, t = 45° perfectly satisfies the equation.

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin²(t) = 1/2 × tan(t)

**Formula Used:**

tan(t) = sin(t) / cos(t)

sin(2t) = 2 × sin(t) × cos(t)

**Calculation:**

⇒ sin²(t) = 1/2 × [sin(t) / cos(t)]

Since t ≠ 0° based on the options, sin(t) will not be zero. We can divide both sides by sin(t):

⇒ sin(t) = 1 / [2 × cos(t)]

Cross-multiplying the terms on both sides:

⇒ 2 × sin(t) × cos(t) = 1

Applying the double angle formula:

⇒ sin(2t) = 1

We know that the principal value of sin(90°) = 1, therefore:

⇒ 2t = 90°

⇒ t = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios at 45°

At 45°, the sine and cosine values are equal. sin(45°) = cos(45°) = 1/√2 | tan(45°) = cot(45°) = 1.

Double Angle Identity for Sine

sin(2θ) = 2 × sin(θ) × cos(θ) = (2 × tan(θ)) / (1 + tan²(θ)).

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 | 1 + tan²(θ) = sec²(θ) | 1 + cot²(θ) = cosec²(θ).
</p

questions.question: If 7 tan θ = 3, and θ is an acute angle, then (5 sin theta - cos theta)/(5 sin theta + 2 cos theta) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given 7 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3/7.

Divide the numerator and denominator of the expression by cos θ to convert it into tan θ terms.

Expression = (5 tan θ − 1) / (5 tan θ + 2)

Value = (5 × 3/7 − 1) / (5 × 3/7 + 2) = (15/7 − 7/7) / (15/7 + 14/7) = 8 / 29

**∴ The correct answer is 8/29.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

7 tan θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = 3/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e47352a8607d277926b9a6505f04db226f7f872748be4d2233a16979a503950a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

By Pythagoras Theorem, Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Perpendicular (AB) = 3 and Base (BC) = 7

⇒ Hypotenuse (AC) = √(3² + 7²) = √(9 + 49) = √58

⇒ sin θ = 3 / √58

⇒ cos θ = 7 / √58

⇒ Expression = (5 sin θ − cos θ) / (5 sin θ + 2 cos θ)

⇒ Substitute the values of sin θ and cos θ

⇒ Numerator = 5 × (3 / √58) − (7 / √58) = (15 − 7) / √58 = 8 / √58

⇒ Denominator = 5 × (3 / √58) + 2 × (7 / √58) = (15 + 14) / √58 = 29 / √58

⇒ Expression Value = (8 / √58) ÷ (29 / √58) = 8 / 29

**∴ The correct answer is 8/29.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular / Base.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: H² = P² + B².

Homogeneous Expressions

When calculating a ratio where both the numerator and denominator are of the same degree in sine and cosine, dividing by a suitable power of cosine directly yields the result in terms of tangent.

questions.question: If sec A = (5)/(4), then the value of (tan A)/(1 + tan²A) - (sin A)/(sec A) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **sec A = 5/4**, which is a **3-4-5 Pythagorean triplet** where **Hypotenuse = 5** and **Base = 4**.

Simplify the expression: tan A / (1 + tan²A) − sin A / sec A.

Using 1 + tan²A = sec²A, the first term becomes: (sin A / cos A) / sec²A = sin A × cos A.

The second term is: sin A / sec A = sin A × cos A.

Result = sin A × cos A − sin A × cos A = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dca8543c26b7e440a2dbeaaff4c99a62354e28a635d9902961adf5f1e551421c.png] 

**Given:** sec A = 5/4 ⇒ H = 5, B = 4

**Formula:** P² = H² − B²; sin A = P/H; tan A = P/B; 1 + tan²A = sec²A

⇒ P = √(5² − 4²) = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3

⇒ sin A = 3/5, cos A = 4/5, tan A = 3/4

⇒ Expression = [ (3/4) / (1 + (3/4)²) ] − [ (3/5) / (5/4) ]

⇒ Expression = [ (3/4) / (1 + 9/16) ] − [ 12/25 ]

⇒ Expression = [ (3/4) / (25/16) ] − 12/25

⇒ Expression = [ (3/4) × (16/25) ] − 12/25

⇒ Expression = 12/25 − 12/25 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²A + cos²A = 1, 1 + tan²A = sec²A, and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A.

Reciprocal Relations

sec A = 1/cos A, cosec A = 1/sin A, and tan A = sin A/cos A.

Double Angle Representation

The expression tan A / (1 + tan²A) is equivalent to (sin A × cos A), which is also (1/2)sin 2A.</p

questions.question: If cos A + cos²A = 1 then sin²A + sin⁴A is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From cos A + cos²A = 1, we directly get cos A = 1 − cos²A = sin²A.

Squaring both sides gives cos²A = sin⁴A.

Substitute these into the required expression: sin²A + sin⁴A.

This transforms into cos A + cos²A, which is already given as 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cos A + cos²A = 1

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos A + cos²A = 1

⇒ cos A = 1 − cos²A

⇒ cos A = sin²A

Now, evaluating the required expression:

⇒ sin²A + sin⁴A

⇒ sin²A + (sin²A)²

Substituting sin²A = cos A into the above expression:

⇒ cos A + (cos A)²

⇒ cos A + cos²A

Since it is already given that cos A + cos²A = 1:

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 ⇒ sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ and cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ.

Secant and Tangent Identity

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ.

Cosecant and Cotangent Identity

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 ⇒ cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ.

Symmetric Pattern Result

If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, then the symmetric expression evaluates to cos²θ + cos⁴θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: ΔEFG is a right angled triangle. ∠F = 90 degree, EF = 10 cm and FG = 15 cm. What is the value of cosec G?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of sides **EF : FG** = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3.

In a right triangle with sides 2 and 3, **Hypotenuse (EG)** = √(2² + 3²) = √13 units.

For ∠G, **Perpendicular** = EF = 2 units and **Hypotenuse** = √13 units.

**cosec G** = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular = √13 / 2.

**∴ The correct answer is √13/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** In ΔEFG, ∠F = 90°, **EF** = 10 cm, **FG** = 15 cm.

**Formula:** **Pythagoras Theorem:** EG² = EF² + FG² | **cosec G** = Hypotenuse / Opposite side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36264dca0903ebdca3276fae850fc3fe3bd1dc2c6adb00b6aba25eea0e4083cd.png] 

⇒ In **ΔEFG**, by **Pythagoras Theorem**:

⇒ EG² = 10² + 15²

⇒ EG² = 100 + 225 = 325

⇒ EG = √325 = √(25 × 13) = 5√13 cm

⇒ **cosec G** = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular (Opposite to G)

⇒ cosec G = EG / EF

⇒ cosec G = (5√13) / 10

⇒ cosec G = √13 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is √13/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratio Definitions

In a **right-angled triangle**, **sin θ** = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, **cos θ** = Base/Hypotenuse, and **tan θ** = Perpendicular/Base.

Reciprocal Relations

**cosec θ** is the reciprocal of **sin θ** (1/sin θ), **sec θ** is the reciprocal of **cos θ** (1/cos θ), and **cot θ** is the reciprocal of **tan θ** (1/tan θ).

Pythagoras Theorem

For any right triangle with legs **a**, **b** and hypotenuse **c**, the relationship is always **a² + b² = c²**.</p
